caption:
When you're stressed, how do you speak to yourself?

Self-compassion means meeting your own hard moments with the kindness you would give a friend. A meta-analysis of trials found programmes that taught it over several weeks were linked with less stress than having no programme. Compared with other approaches, like relaxation training, there was no clear difference. Many of the studies had quality problems.

Some of these programmes included a short practice called a self-compassion break:
1. Name it. "This is a hard moment."
2. Remember you're not alone. Other people feel this too.
3. Offer yourself a kind word, the way you would a friend. "What do I need right now?"
The steps follow mindfulness, common humanity and self-kindness, as described in a trial that used the self-compassion break.

This is a taster, and the programmes ran for weeks. If self-criticism feels heavy, talking it through with a psychologist is an option.

Save this for a hard day.

Research:
Han, A., & Kim, T. H. (2023). Effects of self-compassion interventions on reducing depressive symptoms, anxiety, and stress: A meta-analysis. Mindfulness, 14(7). https://doi.org/10.1007/s12671-023-02148-x
Preuss, H., Capito, K., van Eickels, R. L., Zemp, M., & Kolar, D. R. (2021). Cognitive reappraisal and self-compassion as emotion regulation strategies for parents during COVID-19: An online randomized controlled trial. Internet Interventions, 24, 100388. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.invent.2021.100388
